translations.text: First he advanced against the temple, stripped it, and melted everything down. He took the silver and gold, the weapons and ornaments, and all the equipment for war. He took the hidden treasures that he found and all the precious vessels, and went to his own country.
Whoever does not obey the king’s command shall be put to death.
The sanctuary was delivered into the hands of foreigners, and the temple became like a man fallen from glory.
Those who were forcibly pressing for apostasy came from the king and arrived in the city of Modein to offer sacrifices there.

They began speaking to one another, saying, “If we all follow the example of our brothers, who did not go out to fight against the Gentiles for their lives and their laws, then before long they will destroy us even more quickly than the first ones.”
He circumcised the uncircumcised children and grew strong throughout the territory of the Israelites.
To attend to the law, to take vengeance on the Gentiles, and to abolish the king’s unlawful decree; and they did not allow the horn of arrogance to rise.
Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael were saved by their faith from the fire in the furnace.

When he saw that the treasures were exhausted and the tribute from the country had diminished because of the division and the devastation he had brought upon the land by abolishing the ancestral laws that had existed from the earliest times
They brought the priestly garments, the firstborn offspring, and the tithes into their midst. They roused and brought forward those under vows whose appointed days had been completed.

They saw the sanctuary devastated, the altar defiled, and the gates burned. Bushes were growing throughout the courts as in a forest or on the mountains. The basins were demolished, and the curtain supports were damaged.

In their deliberations there, they resolved to tear down the altar because it had been defiled by their enemies, so that it would not remain a burden on their conscience and an everlasting reproach. And they tore down the altar.
There was exceedingly great joy among the people, and the reproach inflicted by the Gentiles was wiped away from them.
When the surrounding Gentiles heard that the altar had been rebuilt and the sanctuary restored once again as it had been before, they became very angry.
He crossed over and advanced against the Ammonites. There he found a powerful force, many troops, and Timothy their commander.
All the Gentiles in Gilead gathered against the Israelites who lived in their territory, intending to destroy them. The Israelites fled into the stronghold at Dothaim.

While these words were still in his mouth, Judas arrived with his troops at the riverbank. There he stationed the muster clerks along the bank and commanded them not to allow anyone at all to camp beside the river, but to send every fighting man across after him.
They crossed the Jordan River into the level country, onto a broad plain, and camped there opposite Beth-shan.
There Judas looked after the welfare of the people and encouraged everyone. He did this throughout the entire march until he brought them into the land of Judea.
Gorgias came out of the city with the troops who were with him to do battle, and attacked them.
They have raised their hands not only against us, but also throughout all their own territory.
When he returned from Persia and Parthia, all the troops joined him, and he himself wished to take charge of the affairs of the kingdom.
When Antiochus was about to enter the royal palace of his ancestors, many troops surrounded him. They arrested Lysias and Antiochus, bound them, and brought them to Demetrius.
The emperor chose Bacchides, a friend of the king and governor of the region beyond the river, a great official faithful to his kingdom, and they sent him out.
Bacchides set out and went on his way. From where he was, he sent messengers to Judas and his brothers to speak to them about peace with deceitful words.
Bacchides left Jerusalem and came and encamped at Bethzeth. He sent men and seized many of the deserters and many of the people, and ordered them to be slaughtered inside the pit.
About five hundred men fell on Nicanor’s side, and the rest fled into the City of David.
The proposal seemed good to them.
He began to speak to those who remained, saying, “Come, let us attack them head-on. Perhaps we can inflict some damage on them.”

The troops came out from their respective camps and drew up face-to-face against one another. Bacchides’ troops formed two fully armed divisions. The slingers and archers advanced ahead of the division, and the warriors had gone out in front.
The sons of Jambri, who were in Damascus, came out, seized John, and took him and his baggage away with them.

“Now come, let us raise our voices to heaven and charge against them. Perhaps you will escape from the hands of our enemies.” He said these words and immediately joined battle, charging against Bacchides.
The lawless men plotted and said, “Look, Jonathan and those with him are living peacefully and without concern. Now come, let us bring Bacchides, and he will seize them all in a single night.”
Jonathan settled in Jerusalem and began to rebuild and restore the city.
“Now take this, and let us also write to them words of encouragement, honors, and gifts, so that they will come to our aid.”

The two kings came and clashed with one another. Demetrius’ army turned to flee, and Alexander prevailed over them.
They came to the city of Joppa. The citizens shut the gates against them, because guards appointed by Apollonius were stationed over them. They attacked and laid siege to the city.
He went toward the region of Azotus, keeping close to the plain because he trusted in his troops. Jonathan followed him to engage him in battle.
Simon took a secret route with his division, advanced along the ravine, and fell upon them. While they were resting and exhausted, he attacked them and killed many of them there in the ambush.

He confirmed him in the office of high priest and in all the other honors he had previously held. He appointed him among his chief friends.
Jonathan asked the king to exempt Judea, the three districts, and Samaria from tribute, and undertook to give him three hundred talents.

We have established the boundaries of Judea, and the three districts of Ephraim, Lydda, and Ramathaim have been added to Judea from the territory of Samaria. All revenues lawfully due from them shall belong to those serving in Jerusalem, in place of the royal revenues that came from them year by year from the crops of the land and the fruit of the trees.

He hurried to him so that he would give him the child, whom he would bring back and make king in his father's place. He told him everything Demetrius had done and all the hostility the troops had shown. He stayed there with him for many days.

They said these words and each threw down his weapons at the feet of the fighting men. The Israelite force rose in glory before the king and all his troops, and they returned to Jerusalem with great renown and much plunder.
Jonathan heard that Demetrius's commanders had arrived at Kedesh in the territory of Galilee with large forces, intending to remove him from his position.
That day they struck down and killed about three thousand armed horsemen. Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
Onias received the man who had been sent with great honor and took a letter in which he described us as his comrades in arms, supporters, and beloved friends.
For he heard that the fortresses were giving their support to Demetrius, and he stationed guards and officers over them.
Jonathan returned, selected troops, and summoned the council of elders for consultation, wishing to build the fortifications of Judea.
Simon knew that he was speaking deceitfully to him, but he had the silver and the boys sent, lest hostility arise between the people and himself.
Those in the citadel in Jerusalem sent messengers to Tryphon, urging him to come to them through the wilderness and supply the fortress with provisions.
Tryphon dealt treacherously with the young King Antiochus and killed him.
Simon summoned chosen men and sent them to Demetrius so that he would grant the land an exemption, for everything Tryphon did was plunder.
King Demetrius to Simon the high priest, friend of kings, and to the entire council of elders of the Jewish nation: Greetings.
If any of you are suitable and worthy to be entered on our register, let them be entered freely. And let there be peace between us and you.
News reached the city of the Romans and the territory of the Spartans that Jonathan had died, and they were deeply grieved.

In his days he succeeded in wiping out the Gentiles from his land. Those who were in the citadel in Jerusalem would come out and go in, greatly defiling the area around the sanctuary, and great harm was done to the sanctuary. He confined them there and wiped them out.
For the Jews themselves and the priests were pleased to agree to appoint him ruler and high priest forever, until a trustworthy prophet should arise.
The letters were worded as follows: King Antiochus to Simon the great high priest and governor of the Jewish nation: Greetings.

Ptolemy son of Abubus had been appointed over the regions of the plain at Jericho, and he possessed a great deal of silver and gold.

Simon traveled through the districts, caring for them and seeing to their needs. He came down to Jericho, he himself and Mattathias and Judas and his sons, in the one hundred and seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat.
He sent half of them to the region of Gezer to remove John from there. He also wrote to the commanders, telling them to come and receive gold, silver, and many gifts from him.
